Israel. A country in western Asia on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, occupying a narrow strip of land between Lebanon and Egypt known historically as the Levant. Established as a Jewish state in 1948 following the Holocaust and decades of Zionist migration, Israel is the only Jewish-majority nation in the world. Its creation displaced hundreds of thousands of Palestinians and led to a conflict that has defined Middle Eastern politics for over 75 years.

Its territory includes the coastal plains of the Mediterranean, the Jordan River valley to the east, and the Negev Desert to the south. It also occupies the West Bank and Gaza Strip, territories disputed since the 1967 war. Judaism, one of the world's oldest monotheistic religions, originated in ancient Israel over 3,000 years ago. The Torah, Judaism's central text, recounts the history of the Jewish people in the land.

The Zionist movement emerged in the late 19th century, advocating for a Jewish homeland in response to antisemitism in Europe. Mass Jewish immigration to Palestine increased substantially after the Holocaust from 1939 to 1945. Israel was established on May 14, 1948, immediately after the British Mandate ended. The declaration of independence triggered the Arab-Israeli War from 1948 to 1949, with over 700,000 Palestinians fleeing or being expelled.

Jerusalem, the capital claimed by Israel, is one of the world's holiest cities, sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Its status remains the central point of Israeli-Palestinian dispute. Israel's economy is highly developed, with major strengths in technology, agriculture, and diamonds. It has the highest per-capita number of startups of any nation. The Arab-Israeli conflict has involved multiple wars in 1948, 1956, 1967, and 1973, decades of Palestinian uprisings known as intifadas, and ongoing settlement expansion that the international community considers illegal. Israel is home to the Dead Sea, the world's lowest elevation on land at 430 meters below sea level, and the Sea of Galilee, significant to Christian and Jewish history.
